newsitem.title: USA: Weekend rains may skirt dry areas of Illinois--WSC.
newsitem.headline: Weekend rains may skirt dry areas of Illinois--WSC.

text.p: Showers forecast for the U.S. Midwest this weeked may be lightest in the areas where corn and soybean crops most need moisture, Weather Services Corp senior agricultural meteorologist David Taylor said.

"Right now it looks like we will have the hardest time getting decent rain in the Illinois and Indiana area," he said, noting rainfall of 0.25 to 1.00 inch was expected over the weekend in the Midwest with 40 to 60 percent coverage.
The wettest areas should to the north and west of the western corn belt and also to the north and east of the eastern Corn Belt, Taylor said.
WSC's Taylor said the front would be preceded by above normal temperatures with highs in the U.S. Midwest in the upper 80s Fahrenheit and low 90s F.
"Above-normal temperatures are going to place additional stresses on all the crops which there is no question are moisture starved," Taylor said.
Temperatures should then slip back to normal levels with highs in the low to mid 80s F.
Taylor said the next chance of rain in the U.S. Midwest would be the following Thursday or Friday. "That one does not look as good a chance as the present (weekend) one," he noted.
